title: Cap. X Arg. VII: against Christ-death as a cast lot — Isa. liii. 10 promises Christ a church if he lays down his soul as a sacrifice
pass_a_gloss: But whatsoever these hold is utterly alien from Theology, and contrary to the Scriptures: that the death of Christ was as it were a lot cast, so that, his soul having been laid down, whether anyone should be made safe through his death would hang wholly upon the contingency of men’s free will. Far otherwise Isaiah, Isa. liii. 10. If he shall have laid down his soul a sacrifice for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed. God therefore promises unto Christ a Church, if he shall have laid down his soul a sacrifice for sin.
pass_b_english: But whatever they hold is wholly alien to theology and contrary to Scripture: that Christ’s death was like a lot cast, so that—his soul once laid down—whether anyone would be saved by that death hung wholly on the contingency of human free will. Isaiah speaks far otherwise (Isa. liii. 10): If he shall lay down his soul as a sacrifice for sin, he shall see a long-lived seed. So God promises Christ a church if he lays down his soul as a sacrifice for sin.
source_text: At quicquid isti tenent, est prorsus alienum a Theologia, et Scripturis contrarium, mortem Christi fuisse quasi aleam jactam, ita ut posita anima sua, an quisquam per mortem ejus salvus fieret, ex contingentia liberi hominum arbitrii prorsus penderet. Longe aliter Isaias, Isa. liii. 10. Si posuerit animam suam hostiam pro peccato, semen longaevum videbit. Deus igitur promittit Christo Ecclesiam, si animam posuerit hostiam pro peccato.
